name: km/h to m/s conversion
common_traps: Multiplying by 18/5 when converting km/h to m/s (answer about 13 times too small or large).
Mixing m with km/h without converting (track in m, speed in km/h).
Converting each speed but forgetting to add them for opposite directions.

verification.code:
import random
from fractions import Fraction as F
random.seed(0)
n = 0
for _ in range(1500):
    v = F(random.randint(1, 5000), random.randint(1, 8))       # km/h
    ms = v * 1000 / 3600                                        # standard: metres per km / seconds per hour
    assert ms == v * F(5, 18)
    assert ms * F(18, 5) == v
    n += 1
# worked example 2024-09-18_1230_Q12: 36, 54 km/h opposite on 4800 m
rel = (36 + 54) * F(5, 18)
assert rel == 25
t = 4800 / rel
assert t == 192
assert {200, 205, 178} & {t} == set()
print(f"CASES={n}")

name: Relative speed (chase and meeting)
conditions: \text{same direction: } v_1>v_2\ \text{(else the gap never closes)}
derivation: Watch from the slower runner: the chaser gains $v_1-v_2$ every unit of time.
The gap closes when the gain equals it: $(v_1-v_2)t=\text{gap}$.
Moving towards each other, both shrink the distance: $(v_1+v_2)t=d$.
If $v_1=v_2$ in the same direction, the gap stays fixed.
visual_proof: A number line with the chaser at 0 and the runner ahead by the gap; both move right and the chaser closes the gap at the speed difference.
shortcut: Distance the leader runs before being caught $=\text{gap}\times\frac{v_2}{v_1-v_2}$ (speed-ratio units).
common_traps: Adding the speeds in a chase (27 km/h gives about 1.3 min).
Leaving km/h with a gap in metres.
Answering in hours or seconds when minutes are asked.

diagram.alt_text: Number line in metres: policeman starts at 0, thief at 600; after 12 minutes both are at 3000, the policeman having run 3000 m and the thief 2400 m.

verification.code:
import random
from fractions import Fraction as F
random.seed(0)

def catch_time(gap, fast, slow, dt=None):
    # positions: chaser at 0, other at gap; solve fast*t = gap + slow*t
    if fast <= slow:
        return None
    return gap / (fast - slow)

n = 0
for _ in range(1500):
    gap = F(random.randint(1, 5000)); v1 = F(random.randint(1, 200)); v2 = F(random.randint(1, 200))
    t = catch_time(gap, v1, v2)
    if t is not None:
        assert v1 * t == gap + v2 * t                  # same position at time t
    d = F(random.randint(1, 5000))
    tm = d / (v1 + v2)
    assert v1 * tm + v2 * tm == d                      # meeting: distances add to d
    n += 1
# boundary: equal speeds never close the gap; slightly faster does
assert catch_time(F(600), F(12), F(12)) is None
assert catch_time(F(600), F(13), F(12)) == 600
print("BOUNDARY_OK")
# worked example 2024-09-09_1600_Q06: 600 m, 15 vs 12 km/h, answer in minutes
rel = F(15 - 12) * 1000 / 60          # m per min
t = catch_time(F(600), F(15) * 1000 / 60, F(12) * 1000 / 60)
assert rel == 50 and t == 12
assert {8, 10, 15} & {t} == set()
# 2024-09-17_0900_Q14: 72 km, 8 and 10 km/h, meet after combined 144 km
assert 8 * F(144, 18) == 64
print(f"CASES={n}")

name: Speed and time inversely proportional
visual_proof: Two bars of equal distance: the faster one is split into fewer, longer time steps; time ratio is the speed ratio flipped.
shortcut: Swap the ratio: times $a:b$ over the same distance mean speeds $b:a$.

steps: Same distance, times down : up $=18:36$, so speeds down : up $=36:18=2:1$.

common_traps: Keeping the time ratio as the speed ratio (down : up = 1 : 2) gives an impossible negative stream.
Answering the downstream : upstream ratio 2 : 1 instead of boat : stream.
Using the ratio rule when the distances differ.

diagram.alt_text: Table: downstream takes 18 h, upstream 36 h over the same distance, so speeds are 2 and 1 units; boat 1.5, stream 0.5.

import random
from fractions import Fraction as F
random.seed(0)
n = 0
for _ in range(1500):
    d = F(random.randint(1, 10**4)); v1 = F(random.randint(1, 300)); v2 = F(random.randint(1, 300))
    t1, t2 = d / v1, d / v2
    assert t1 / t2 == v2 / v1
    t = F(random.randint(1, 100), random.randint(1, 6))
    assert (v1 * t) / (v2 * t) == v1 / v2
    n += 1
# worked example 2024-09-17_1230_Q12: down 18 h, up 36 h -> D : U = 36 : 18 = 2 : 1 -> b : s = 3 : 1
D, U = F(36), F(18)
b, s = (D + U) / 2, (D - U) / 2
assert b / s == 3
assert {F(3, 2), F(2), F(2, 3)} & {b / s} == set()
print(f"CASES={n}")

name: Meeting on a circular track
statement: t_{\text{first meet}}=\frac{L}{|v_1\mp v_2|}\ (- \text{ same direction},\ + \text{ opposite});\ \text{at start: } \mathrm{LCM}\left(\tfrac L{v_1},\tfrac L{v_2}\right)
derivation: Same direction: they meet again when the faster has gained one full lap $L$ on the slower.
Opposite directions: they meet when together they have covered one lap, $t=\frac L{v_1+v_2}$.
Both back at the start together: a whole number of laps each, so $t=\mathrm{LCM}$ of the lap times $\frac L{v_1}$ and $\frac L{v_2}$.
visual_proof: The track unrolled into a straight line of length L: the gap between the runners grows at the relative speed and they meet each time it reaches a full lap.
shortcut: Same direction: time $=\frac{L}{\text{difference}}$; opposite: $\frac{L}{\text{sum}}$; convert km/h with $\times\frac5{18}$ first.

steps: Faster gains one lap of 840 m: $t=\frac{840}6=140$ s (A).

common_traps: Adding speeds for the same direction (840/18 ≈ 46.7 s).
Using the LCM of lap times (140 s here by coincidence, but generally the meeting at the start point, not the first meeting).
Not converting km/h to m/s when the track is in metres.

diagram.alt_text: Gap between the runners growing at 6 m/s from 0 to the full 840 m lap at 140 seconds, when they meet.

segments.label: gap grows 6 m/s → one lap at 140 s

verification.code:
import random
from math import gcd
from fractions import Fraction as F
random.seed(0)

def first_meet(L, v1, v2, same):
    rel = abs(v1 - v2) if same else v1 + v2
    return None if rel == 0 else F(L) / rel

def brute(L, v1, v2, same):
    # smallest t > 0 with positions equal mod L; the gap changes by rel*t, meet when it is a multiple of L
    rel = abs(v1 - v2) if same else v1 + v2
    if rel == 0:
        return None
    # check candidate times k*L/rel: first k that works is 1, and nothing smaller works
    t = F(L, 1) / rel
    p1, p2 = (v1 * t) % L, ((v2 if same else -v2) * t) % L
    assert p1 == p2
    for j in range(1, 24):                  # no earlier meeting on a grid of 23 earlier times
        tt = t * j / 24
        assert (v1 * tt) % L != ((v2 if same else -v2) * tt) % L
    return t

def lcm_frac(a, b):
    num = a.numerator * b.denominator; den = a.denominator * b.numerator
    g = gcd(num, den)
    return a * (den // g)

n = 0
for _ in range(1500):
    L = random.randint(100, 5000); v1 = random.randint(1, 40); v2 = random.randint(1, 40)
    same = random.random() < 0.5
    assert first_meet(L, v1, v2, same) == brute(L, v1, v2, same)
    # meeting at the start point: LCM of the lap times
    if v1 != v2:
        T = lcm_frac(F(L, v1), F(L, v2))
        assert (T * v1) % L == 0 and (T * v2) % L == 0
        for k in range(1, 50):
            tt = T / k
            if k > 1:
                assert (tt * v1) % L != 0 or (tt * v2) % L != 0
    n += 1
# boundary: equal speeds in the same direction never meet again
assert first_meet(840, 6, 6, True) is None
assert first_meet(840, 6, 6, False) == 70
print("BOUNDARY_OK")
# worked example 2024-09-09_0900_Q03: 840 m, 6 and 12 m/s, same direction
t = first_meet(840, 6, 12, True)
assert t == 140
assert {40, 70, 20} & {t} == set()
print(f"CASES={n}")

name: Boats and streams
conditions: b>s\ \text{(else the boat cannot move upstream)}
visual_proof: Downstream bar = boat speed plus stream; upstream bar = boat speed minus stream; still water is midway between them.
shortcut: Still-water speed is the average of $D$ and $U$; stream speed is half their difference.

steps: 6 km in still water: $\frac64=1.5$ h $=1$ hr 30 min (A).

common_traps: Using the stream speed $\frac{6-2}2=2$ as the boat speed (gives 3 h).
Taking 1 km in 10 min as 1 km/h, or 10 km/h, instead of 6 km/h.
Using downstream speed for still water (gives 1 h).

diagram.alt_text: Bars: downstream 6 km/h made of boat 4 plus stream 2; upstream 2 km/h equals boat 4 minus stream 2; still water 4 km/h.

verification.code:
import random
from fractions import Fraction as F
random.seed(0)
n = 0
for _ in range(1500):
    b = F(random.randint(2, 400), 4); s = F(random.randint(0, int(b * 4) - 1), 4)
    assert s < b
    D, U = b + s, b - s
    assert (D + U) / 2 == b and (D - U) / 2 == s
    n += 1
# boundary: b = s -> upstream speed 0, the boat cannot go up
def upstream_time(d, b, s):
    return None if b - s <= 0 else d / (b - s)
assert upstream_time(F(10), F(5), F(5)) is None        # b = s: never gets upstream
assert upstream_time(F(10), F(5), F(4)) == 10           # b just above s: finite
print("BOUNDARY_OK")
# worked example 2024-09-12_1600_Q13: up 2 km in 1 h, down 1 km in 10 min
U, D = F(2), F(1) / F(10, 60)
b = (D + U) / 2
t = 6 / b
assert D == 6 and b == 4 and t == F(3, 2)          # 1 h 30 min
assert {F(5, 4), F(5, 2), F(7, 4)} & {t} == set()
print(f"CASES={n}")

name: Trains crossing
derivation: Crossing starts when the fronts meet and ends when the rears separate.
Relative to the other train, one train must cover both lengths: $L_1+L_2$.
$t=\frac{L_1+L_2}{v_1\pm v_2}$; a pole or man has $L_2=0$, $v_2=0$; a platform has $v_2=0$.
visual_proof: Two trains side by side on parallel tracks: the distance to clear is the two lengths laid end to end, covered at the relative speed.
shortcut: Same-direction and opposite times $t_s,t_o$ give $v_1-v_2=\frac{L_1+L_2}{t_s}$ and $v_1+v_2=\frac{L_1+L_2}{t_o}$.

steps: Towards each other: relative speed $=32+40=72$ km/h $=20$ m/s.

common_traps: Using only one train's length (132/20 = 6.6 s).
Subtracting speeds for trains moving towards each other (240/(8×5/18) = 108 s).
Forgetting the km/h to m/s conversion.

diagram.alt_text: Distance line of 240 m made of the 132 m train and the 108 m train, covered at 20 m/s in 12 s.

verification.code:
import random
from fractions import Fraction as F
random.seed(0)

def cross_time(L1, L2, v1, v2, same):
    rel = abs(v1 - v2) if same else v1 + v2
    return None if rel == 0 else (L1 + L2) / rel

def simulate(L1, L2, v1, v2, same):
    # front of train 1 meets front/rear of train 2; crossing ends when rear of 1 clears the far end of 2
    # in train 2's frame, train 1 moves at the relative speed and must travel L1 + L2
    rel = abs(v1 - v2) if same else v1 + v2
    if rel == 0:
        return None
    pos_rear1 = -L1                 # rear of train 1 starts L1 behind the contact point
    target = L2                     # must pass the far end of train 2
    return (target - pos_rear1) / rel

n = 0
for _ in range(1500):
    L1, L2 = F(random.randint(50, 600)), F(random.randint(0, 600))
    v1, v2 = F(random.randint(1, 50)), F(random.randint(0, 50))
    same = random.random() < 0.5
    assert cross_time(L1, L2, v1, v2, same) == simulate(L1, L2, v1, v2, same)
    n += 1
# boundary: equal speeds in the same direction never cross; a pole/man is L2 = 0, v2 = 0
assert cross_time(F(100), F(100), F(20), F(20), True) is None
assert cross_time(F(100), F(0), F(20), F(0), True) == 5
print("BOUNDARY_OK")
# worked example 2024-09-24_1230_Q05: 132 m and 108 m, 32 and 40 km/h towards each other
t = cross_time(F(132), F(108), F(32) * F(5, 18), F(40) * F(5, 18), False)
assert t == 12
assert {15, 10, 13} & {t} == set()
# 2024-09-19_0900_Q21: 400 m, same dir 20 s, opposite 5 s -> 180 and 108 km/h
a = (F(400, 20) + F(400, 5)) / 2; b = (F(400, 5) - F(400, 20)) / 2
assert a * F(18, 5) == 180 and b * F(18, 5) == 108
print(f"CASES={n}")

name: Average speed over equal distances
derivation: Two equal distances $d$: time $=\frac d{v_1}+\frac d{v_2}$.
$\bar v=\frac{2d}{\frac d{v_1}+\frac d{v_2}}=\frac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}$, the harmonic mean.
visual_proof: Three equal stretches of road with the time each takes: the slow stretch takes longest, so the average is pulled below the simple mean.
shortcut: Take the distance as the LCM of the speeds, add the times, divide.
common_traps: Taking the simple average (40 + 50 + 60)/3 = 50 km/h.
Using the two-speed formula on three parts.
Applying the harmonic mean when equal times (not distances) are given.

diagram.alt_text: Distance 600 km split into three 200 km thirds taking 5 h at 40, 4 h at 50 and 10/3 h at 60 km/h; total 37/3 h.

verification.code:
import random
from fractions import Fraction as F
random.seed(0)
n = 0
for _ in range(1500):
    v1, v2 = F(random.randint(1, 300)), F(random.randint(1, 300))
    d = F(random.randint(1, 1000))
    avg = 2 * d / (d / v1 + d / v2)                  # total distance / total time
    assert avg == 2 * v1 * v2 / (v1 + v2)
    k = random.randint(2, 5)
    vs = [F(random.randint(1, 300)) for _ in range(k)]
    assert k * d / sum(d / v for v in vs) == k / sum(1 / v for v in vs)
    n += 1
# boundary: v1 = v2 gives the same speed; harmonic mean is below the arithmetic mean otherwise
assert 2 * F(40) * 40 / (40 + 40) == 40
assert 2 * F(40) * 60 / (40 + 60) < 50
print("BOUNDARY_OK")
# worked example 2024-09-10_0900_Q17: thirds at 40, 50, 60 km/h
avg = 3 / (F(1, 40) + F(1, 50) + F(1, 60))
assert avg == F(3600, 74)
assert round(float(avg), 2) == 48.65
assert all(abs(float(avg) - o) > 0.1 for o in (54.13, 51.43, 46.85))
print(f"CASES={n}")
